question.text: Delivery period margin for Options on Goods is charged:

answer.text: On both buyers and sellers of ITM, CTM, or expected ITM/CTM positions in Options on Goods during the last 3-5 days before expiry
Never — options don't have delivery margins
Only after the option is exercised

explanation.text: The Logic: For Options on Goods, delivery period margin is charged on both buyers and sellers of ITM, CTM, or expected ITM/CTM positions during the last 3-5 days before expiry, since those positions are likely to result in delivery obligations. The Trap: Limiting delivery period margin to sellers only is incorrect for Options on Goods — buyers of ITM/CTM positions are also covered. Seller-only treatment fits Short Option Minimum Margin (SOMM), a different charge. Note: The 3-5 day window before expiry is the standard reference period during which the delivery-related margin builds up on these positions.
